rows.name: VFW Voices of Democracy - Patriotic Audio Essay “How Are You Showing Patriotism And Support For Our Country?”
values: VFW Veterans of Foreign Wars Information
VFW Voices of Democracy - Patriotic Audio Essay “How Are You Showing Patriotism And Support For Our Country?”

All entries must start with the local VFW post. Contact the Whitefish VFW to see about participating. Record your original 3-5 minute (+ or – 5 second max.) audio essay on a flash drive, or other electronic device. Hearing/speech impaired students should email the Voice of Democracy National Office at youth scholarships@vfw.org for special instructions. No music, singing, poetry or sound effects are allowed. The body of the essay must not identify you in any way, (including, but not limited to your name, school, city, state, race, or national origin) although the recording & typed essay should be labeled with your name, to show ownership. All entries competing at the local Post level must be in the hands of that VFW Post by midnight, Oct. 31, 2025.  Originality is worth 35 points (treatment of the theme should show imagination and human interest), Content is worth 30 points (clearly express your ideas in an organized manner. Fully develop your theme and use transitions to move smoothly from one idea to another), Delivery is worth 35 points (speak in a clear and credible manner). Read application for further details. You will submit the recording, typed essay and this completed entry form to: Dustin Wegner, Commander     20 Baker Ave., Whitefish, MT  59937 (you can mail or drop off in person). Call Dustin Wegner with questions: 406.654.4020

rows.name: Hagan Scholarship
values: The Hagan Scholarship is a nationwide need-based merit scholarship, designed to provide recipients with the opportunity to graduate college debt-free. Applicants must attend a traditional public high school governed by a school district. Free workshops, Free Schwab Brokerage Accounts and Free Study Abroad provide recipients with a practical understanding of important life skills not typically covered in the school curriculum. (Hagan Scholarship Brochure). Applicant’s Adjusted Gross Household Income reported for 2023 Federal Income Tax Purposes must not have exceeded $100,000. “Household Income” is defined as the total income received by all members of a household living under the same roof. Applicants must show evidence they will be working 240 hours from January 1, 2026 to September 1, 2026 (they understand that most recipients work during the summer months. Work can be part-time during their senior year in high school or full-time during the summer or a combination of the two. They are looking for "students willing to contribute toward their educational expenses."

rows.name: KIITA Foundation ($10,000 - Renewable for up to 4 Years!)
values: KIITA Foundation ($10,000 - Renewable for up to 4 Years!)

JUST FOR WHITEFISH STUDENTS!!! The Kiita Foundation Scholarship (Kiita rhymes with cheetah) was established in 2023 by Jim and Jo-Ann Armstrong. They want to help a high achieving, financially independent student achieve a bachelor's degree. By financially independent, we mean someone who cannot rely on their family to help pay for college.  This award is very generous... up to $10,000 per year and renewable for up to 4 years. The recipient also has the opportunity to participate in all-expense paid service learning trips to Mexico with a cohort of other students.  They are looking for someone who is highly engaged in school and community activities. Again, they need to be financially independent when it comes to paying for college.  
The following essay questions: 1) This scholarship is for students who cannot rely on their family to help pay for college. Please explain why you need the assistance of this scholarship. 2) Please describe any obstacles in your path to high school graduation and how you have overcome them. 3) Please describe why you are interested in pursuing a bachelor’s degree and what you believe you are capable of achieving once you have earned your degree. You may explain this in terms of your life goals, career goals, and/or goals within your community. 4) Describe volunteer activities in which you have chosen to participate, why you chose those particular volunteer activities, and how those experiences have affected your life. Please contact Jill Seigmund at Whitefish Community Foundation with questions: (406) 863-1781 or jill@whitefishcommunityfoundation.org

rows.name: KIITA Foundation ($10,000 - Renewable for up to 4 Years!)
values: KIITA Foundation ($10,000 - Renewable for up to 4 Years!)

JUST FOR WHITEFISH STUDENTS!!! The Kiita Foundation Scholarship (Kiita rhymes with cheetah) was established in 2023 by Jim and Jo-Ann Armstrong. They want to help a high achieving, financially independent student achieve a bachelor's degree. By financially independent, we mean someone who cannot rely on their family to help pay for college.  This award is very generous... up to $10,000 per year and renewable for up to 4 years. The recipient also has the opportunity to participate in all-expense paid service learning trips to Mexico with a cohort of other students.  They are looking for someone who is highly engaged in school and community activities. Again, they need to be financially independent when it comes to paying for college.  
The following essay questions: 1) This scholarship is for students who cannot rely on their family to help pay for college. Please explain why you need the assistance of this scholarship. 2) Please describe any obstacles in your path to high school graduation and how you have overcome them. 3) Please describe why you are interested in pursuing a bachelor’s degree and what you believe you are capable of achieving once you have earned your degree. You may explain this in terms of your life goals, career goals, and/or goals within your community. 4) Describe volunteer activities in which you have chosen to participate, why you chose those particular volunteer activities, and how those experiences have affected your life. Please contact Jill Seigmund at Whitefish Community Foundation with questions: (406) 863-1781 or jill@whitefishcommunityfoundation.org

values: KIITA Foundation ($10,000 - Renewable for up to 4 Years!)

JUST FOR WHITEFISH STUDENTS!!! The Kiita Foundation Scholarship (Kiita rhymes with cheetah) was established in 2023 by Jim and Jo-Ann Armstrong. After review of resumes, each local chapter will conduct brief interviews to determine a nominee who will, in turn, complete an online application to P.E.O. International for final consideration. The online application process can start as early as August 15 but no later than October 15. Nominees are notified of the outcome in mid-April of their senior year.

Funds can be used for flight training such as private pilot, instrument, multiengine, commercial, instructor, or ATP certificates. Applicants must have a high school diploma, be at least 18, and have enrolled in private pilot ground school or logged flight time. Requires addressing specific questions in the essay.
Flight Training (Private, Instrument, Multiengine, Commercial, Instructor, ATP)
rows.rationale: Current official WAI2027 guide names this award; provider and program distinguish it from other associations and direct sponsor awards. Full Master comparison contains no WAI destination. Flight training for private, instrument, multi-engine, commercial, instructor or ATP; excludes sport/recreational certificates. Explain career benefit, why applying and WAI involvement. Older 2025 age/diploma/ground-school restrictions are not restated in the current guide and are not carried forward. Historical values, cycles and statuses remain preserved in the source snapshot.

values: The Anne Bridge Baddour Aviation Scholarship

Awards $5,000 to a female U.S. citizen pilot dedicated to becoming a professional pilot. Must have at least a private pilot certificate with 150 hours of flying time and be on track toward earning the ATP. Award is for instrument rating, multi-engine rating, or ATP.
Professional Pilot, Instrument Rating, Multi-Engine Rating, ATP

values: Delta Air Lines Propel Pilot Scholarship

Awards two $5,000 scholarships to WAI members currently participating in Delta’s Propel Program (collegiate, company, or community partner path). Includes a trip to the WAI2025 conference. Intended for women seeking advancement in professional aviation development toward a career as a professional airline pilot.

rows.name: FedEx Flight Training Scholarship
values: Awards a $5,000 scholarship to a female WAI member pursuing her dream in aviation. Can be used toward an instrument or multiengine rating, commercial or CFI certificate. Funds are paid directly to the flight school and training must be completed within one year. Applicant must have a current private pilot certificate.
Flight Training, Instrument Rating, Multiengine Rating, Commercial Certificate, CFI Certificate
rows.rationale: Current official WAI2027 guide names this award; provider and program distinguish it from other associations and direct sponsor awards. rows.name: Frontier Airlines Flight Training Scholarship
values: Awards a $5,000 scholarship for a female seeking a career as a professional airline pilot. Applicant must be a full-time junior, senior, or graduate student enrolled in an accredited collegiate aviation or aeronautical science program. Requires a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA and FAA Instrument rating; Commercial Certificate and Multi-Engine Rating preferred. Funds paid to flight school, training completed within one year.
rows.rationale: Current official WAI2027 guide names this award; provider and program distinguish it from other associations and direct sponsor awards. Full Master comparison contains no WAI destination. Female full-time college junior, senior or graduate student in accredited aviation/aeronautical science; GPA 3.0 and instrument rating required, commercial/multi-engine preferred. Outside entry-level high-school-to-postsecondary audience. Historical values, cycles and statuses remain preserved in the source snapshot.

rows.name: ISA+21 Financial Scholarship 2025
values: International Society of Women Airline Pilots (ISA+21)

Funds are paid directly to an accredited college/university with an aviation curriculum, an aviation technical school, or a government-approved flight school. Training must be completed within one year of the award.
rows.rationale: Current official WAI2027 guide names this award; provider and program distinguish it from other associations and direct sponsor awards. rows.name: PSA Airlines Flight Scholarship
values: Provides a $3,000 scholarship to a WAI member pursuing a career in commercial aviation as a professional pilot. Candidates must hold a private pilot license and display characteristics of being driven, reliable, and caring, with a passion for aviation.
rows.rationale: Current official WAI2027 guide names this award; provider and program distinguish it from other associations and direct sponsor awards. Full Master comparison contains no WAI destination. Commercial pilot license and working toward CFI; professional airline career goal, driven/reliable/caring qualities. This WAI fund is distinct from the NGPA PSA award. Historical values, cycles and statuses remain preserved in the source snapshot.

rows.name: Republic Airways Opportunity Elevated Scholarship
values: Awards a $5,000 scholarship to a female commercial pilot pursuing a professional pilot career. Candidates are evaluated on academic standing, accomplishments, teamwork, leadership skills, and airmanship. Applicants must be RJet Cadets with Republic Airways.

rows.name: Russ Cotney and Lauren Cotney Professional Airline Pilot Career Scholarship
values: Russ Cotney and Lauren Cotney Professional Airline Pilot Career Scholarship

Preference for veterans, current service members, or daughters of veterans/service members. Requires minimum 3.0 GPA, two letters of recommendation, and an essay detailing goals, achievements, and community involvement.

values: Sun Country Airlines “Fly in a New Direction” Scholarship

Funds are paid directly to the flight school and must be used within a year.
rows.rationale: Current official WAI2027 guide names this award; provider and program distinguish it from other associations and direct sponsor awards. Applicant must be able to read, write, speak, and understand English, have a high school diploma or GED, and be at least 21 years old. Funds are paid directly to the dispatch school.

values: Universal Weather & Aviation FAA-Certified Dispatcher Training Course Scholarship

Travel, lodging, or examiner’s fees are not included.

This training program will impart conceptual knowledge through academics and consolidate that knowledge through training in a Flight Simulation Training Device (FSTD). The course bridges the knowledge gap between a pilot who holds a private pilot certificate and a pilot operating in an air carrier environment. Training must be scheduled to commence no later than one year from the award.

fields.oldValue: The Pell Promise for Montana Students is a financial aid initiative by Carroll College for Montana residents who are Federal Pell Grant recipients. It provides significant financial assistance, covering tuition, to eligible students who maintain a 3.0 GPA, reside on-campus, and accept a federal Stafford loan. It aims to enhance accessibility and affordability for under-served Montanans pursuing a Catholic, liberal arts education.
fields.newValue: The current Carroll Pell Promise page describes fall 2027 first-time freshmen and transfer students residing in the U.S., living on campus, qualifying for Pell through FAFSA, maintaining a 3.0 GPA and completing at least 12 credits per semester, for up to eight semesters. Tuition support combines federal aid, Carroll merit/need gift aid and subsidized Stafford borrowing; it is not all grant funding or a guarantee of full tuition. The introductory steps say to agree to borrow $3,500, while detailed criteria assume maximum subsidized loans of $3,500/$4,500/$5,500 by year; this wording difference remains unresolved. Summer/winter tuition, study abroad and fees are excluded; additional criteria and athletic-aid exceptions may apply. These current 2027 terms differ from the unavailable historical Montana-only 2026 page.

Requires U.S. citizenship, critical financial need, perseverance through adversity, and activity involvement; recipients maintain a 2.0 GPA. Apply by February 15 (applications open December 1).
fields.newValue: The Dennis & Phyllis Washington Foundation's Horatio Alger Montana Undergraduate Scholarship provides up to $15,000 over four years for students who have overcome adversity. Its detailed eligibility still specifies full-time Montana high-school seniors graduating in spring/summer 2026, entering the Montana University System no later than the following fall, US citizenship, critical financial need, integrity/perseverance and co-curricular, after-school or community activity involvement. Pell-eligible families are encouraged; Pell eligibility is not stated as mandatory. Recipients must pursue and complete a bachelor's degree but may start at a two-year institution and transfer. Eligible institutions include UM, MSU and the named Montana affiliates. The page gives December 1–February 15 for seniors and December 1–March 1 for juniors; junior eligibility details and the next cycle year are not fully stated. Apply through Horatio Alger; an existing National Scholarship application is automatically considered. Recipients maintain a 2.0 GPA to keep the award; this is a renewal condition, not a verified entrance minimum. The current page does not substantiate the older $10,000 plus $5,000 split.

fields.newValue: Soroptimist Live Your Dream Awards are for women who provide primary financial support for themselves and their dependents and have financial need. Applicants must be enrolled in or accepted to a vocational/skills training or undergraduate degree program and be motivated to achieve their education and career goals. High-school-equivalency study alone is not listed as an eligible program. Dependents may include children, spouse, partner, siblings or parents. Applicants must reside in a Soroptimist International of the Americas member country or territory, including the United States; previous Women's Opportunity or Live Your Dream recipients, people with or pursuing a graduate degree, Soroptimist members, employees and their immediate family are ineligible. Applications run August 1–November 15 (cycle year not stated). Club awards vary; selected recipients may progress to regional and international levels, for a potential total of $1,000–$16,000. Written sections must reflect the applicant's own experiences and goals; AI may help grammar or organization. Apply through the official Soroptimist application portal.

fields.newValue: Montana STEM/Healthcare Scholarship Program is for Montana residents applying in the year they graduate from a high school accredited by the Montana Board of Public Education. It requires at least a 3.25 cumulative high-school GPA, four years of college-prep math and three years of college-prep science. Students must be accepted at an eligible campus, declare a qualifying STEM or healthcare major, seek their first certificate, two-year or four-year degree, enroll in at least 12 credits each semester and begin in the fall immediately after graduation. Apply through AwardMontana by March 15 (cycle year not stated), with the seventh-semester transcript, acceptance proof and counselor-signed math/science certification. Awards are $1,000 in year one, $1,500 in years two and three and $2,000 in year four if continuing requirements are met; not every program necessarily lasts four years.

Beginning in 2026, the former Joseph James Morelli Legacy Foundation scholarship is available only to students attending Montana State University. The foundation states that it is dissolving and transferring to MSU, which will award the four-year Hilleman/Morelli Scholarship to STEM students demonstrating learning differences, selected for academic, leadership and career potential. It combines financial, academic, leadership and mentoring support. The foundation directs applicants to the Hilleman Scholars application page, whose public instructions reference students starting MSU in Fall 2026. The application extraction did not expose Morelli-specific instructions. A Morelli-specific award amount, deadline, GPA minimum, learning-difference documentation standard, Montana residency requirement, renewal conditions and next-cycle availability are not verified. The foundation historically served students with dyslexia, but the new award uses broader learning-differences wording. This is a distinct named program from the general Hilleman scholarship; its conditions and amount must not be assumed identical.

fields.proposedCorrectionValue: The current Carroll Pell Promise page describes fall 2027 first-time freshmen and transfer students residing in the U.S., living on campus, qualifying for Pell through FAFSA, maintaining a 3.0 GPA and completing at least 12 credits per semester, for up to eight semesters. Tuition support combines federal aid, Carroll merit/need gift aid and subsidized Stafford borrowing; it is not all grant funding or a guarantee of full tuition. The introductory steps say to agree to borrow $3,500, while detailed criteria assume maximum subsidized loans of $3,500/$4,500/$5,500 by year; this wording difference remains unresolved. Summer/winter tuition, study abroad and fees are excluded; additional criteria and athletic-aid exceptions may apply. These current 2027 terms differ from the unavailable historical Montana-only 2026 page.

fields.proposedCorrectionValue: The NCCER/Build Your Future contribution funds the same AGC Workforce Development scholarship represented at Master row 144. Awards are up to $1,000 per year and renewable for up to two years, subject to continuing enrollment and good standing (2.5 GPA or equivalent). Students including high school seniors may pursue approved accredited construction degrees, certificates, craft training or registered apprenticeships full- or part-time; U.S. citizenship or permanent residency is required. The 2026–27 application is closed and requires a fall 2026 class. Its June 1 deadline time conflicts between the form header and body; no time is accepted as settled.

fields.candidateValue: The Dell Scholars program provides financial assistance, academic advising, and career coaching to 500 students nationwide each year. It aims to help students earn their bachelor's degree by offering a flexible scholarship for tuition, housing, books, and living expenses. Eligibility requires being a high school senior in an approved college readiness program, planning to enroll full-time in a four-year college, being Pell Grant eligible, and having a minimum 2.4 GPA.
fields.masterValue: A $20,000 scholarship (plus laptop, textbook credits, and emergency aid) for Pell-eligible high-school seniors who participated in an approved college-readiness program in grades 11-12 and plan to enroll full-time at a four-year college. Rewards persistence over grades — minimum GPA is 2.4. Due February 15. Note the gate: you must have been in an approved college-readiness / college-access program.

Only the first 700 complete applications are reviewed, so apply early.

fields.candidateValue: The Hagan Scholarship is a nationwide need-based merit scholarship for high-achieving rural students graduating from public high schools in counties with fewer than 50,000 residents. It provides financial aid to help recipients attend eligible four-year colleges or universities and graduate debt-free, with potential for graduate school support.
fields.masterValue: The Hagan Scholarship is a nationwide need-based merit scholarship, designed to provide recipients with the opportunity to graduate college debt-free. Applicants must attend a traditional public high school governed by a school district. Free workshops, Free Schwab Brokerage Accounts and Free Study Abroad provide recipients with a practical understanding of important life skills not typically covered in the school curriculum. (Hagan Scholarship Brochure). Applicant’s Adjusted Gross Household Income reported for 2023 Federal Income Tax Purposes must not have exceeded $100,000. “Household Income” is defined as the total income received by all members of a household living under the same roof. Applicants must show evidence they will be working 240 hours from January 1, 2026 to September 1, 2026 (they understand that most recipients work during the summer months. Work can be part-time during their senior year in high school or full-time during the summer or a combination of the two. They are looking for "students willing to contribute toward their educational expenses."
